One of the most common concerns I heard in the district during our town hall tour was about data centers and AI. We need national standards regarding data centers so that we protect our water, air, and quality of life
#paulbarringerforcongress #paulbarringerfornc13 #ncpol https://t.co/uRJi8WCwju

I believe we need national standards for centers to protect our water, air, and overall quality of life. [...] I believe that, as a nation, we could benefit from more time to understand the impacts of AI advancements on our country. We need to make sure we protect our environment and people's jobs. I don’t believe AI is going away, but we need to ensure AI capabilities and data centers are developed responsibly.

And we're not going to put AI back in the bottle, but the impacts that AI and unconstrained, unrestrained growth, particularly of AI data centers, has on our communities is something that we need to be mindful of, especially given the absolutely enormous sums of money that the tech companies have that they're putting towards developing data centers in rural communities, including across District 13. So that's why I think that Congress has a role and the federal government has a role in creating standards around data centers. I think it's appropriate to have a pause, right? Let the people catch up a little bit because the companies have so much money, so much economic power.

So I think it's appropriate for there to be federal standards around how AI data centers, particularly the hyperscale data centers, should be created to minimize the impacts on the environments. But then also, I think people have a lot of concerns about what AI is going to do to employment, to the economy, to people's ability to have a life, right? So I think it's a fair consideration. I think it's a fair for us to have a pause around the development of, especially the hyperscale data centers, just to give the people a chance to catch up.

I think that's one of the biggest things that was concerning about what happened with Doge at the beginning of last year was that they grabbed access to incredible amounts of data. And then that aligned with the companies that they were contracting with that have tremendous AI models and computing power.

We need strong and enforced regulations in regard to AI development. Laws designed specifically to responsibly develop this technology before the creature escapes the lab.
